title: Solve calibration equations
scope: Unique bounded 2×2 systems; no general solver claim

items.prompt: A temperature sensor follows r = c0 + c1·T, where c0 is the offset (mV) and c1 is the gain (mV/°C). Calibration gives r = 5 mV at T = 1 °C and r = 11 mV at T = 3 °C. Find c0 and c1. Enter exact values as decimals or fractions such as 3/8; tolerance ±0.001.
items.solution: Equations: c0 + c1 = 5 and c0 + 3c1 = 11. Subtracting the first from the second gives 2c1 = 6, so c1 = 3 mV/°C. Then c0 = 5 - 3 = 2 mV. Check: 2 + 3·3 = 11.
hints: Each calibration point gives one linear equation in the same two unknowns c0 and c1, so solve the two equations together.
Write c0 + 1·c1 = 5 and c0 + 3·c1 = 11, then subtract the first equation from the second to eliminate c0.
Equations: c0 + c1 = 5 and c0 + 3c1 = 11. Subtracting the first from the second gives 2c1 = 6, so c1 = 3 mV/°C. Then c0 = 5 - 3 = 2 mV. Check: 2 + 3·3 = 11.
items.remediation: If you got c1 = 11/3 you ignored the offset c0 (11 = 3·c1); c0 = 5 means you dropped the gain term. Both points share the same offset and gain; subtract the equations to remove c0. Revisit /lessons/M04.

items.prompt: The same sensor model r = c0 + c1·T (c0 offset in mV, c1 gain in mV/°C) is recalibrated at r = 1 mV for T = -2 °C and r = 10 mV for T = 4 °C. Find c0 and c1. Enter exact values as decimals or fractions such as 3/8; tolerance ±0.001.
items.solution: Subtracting gives (4 - (-2))·c1 = 10 - 1, so 6c1 = 9 and c1 = 1.5 mV/°C. Then c0 = 1 + 2·1.5 = 4 mV. Check: 4 + 4·1.5 = 10.
hints: One calibration temperature is negative; keep its sign as the coefficient of c1.
Write c0 - 2·c1 = 1 and c0 + 4·c1 = 10, then subtract the first equation from the second to get an equation in c1 alone.
Subtracting gives (4 - (-2))·c1 = 10 - 1, so 6c1 = 9 and c1 = 1.5 mV/°C. Then c0 = 1 + 2·1.5 = 4 mV. Check: 4 + 4·1.5 = 10.
items.remediation: If you got c1 = 4.5 you treated T = -2 °C as +2 °C, so 4 - 2 replaced 4 - (-2). Keep the sign of every temperature. Revisit /lessons/M04.

items.prompt: Two strain-gauge channels have crosstalk. With true signals x and y (V), channel 1 reads 2x + 3y and channel 2 reads 5x - 2y. The readings are 4.5 V and 6.5 V. Recover x and y. Enter exact values as decimals or fractions such as 3/8; tolerance ±0.001.
hints: Neither unknown has coefficient 1 in both equations, so scale the equations before eliminating one unknown.
Multiply the channel-1 equation by 2 and the channel-2 equation by 3, so the y-terms become +6y and -6y, then add the equations.
items.remediation: If you got x = 2.25 or 1.3 you solved each channel as if it saw only one signal. Each reading mixes x and y, so the two equations must be solved together. Revisit /lessons/M04.

items.prompt: Two thrusters take signed commands x and y (N). Their allocation gives a net surge force x + y = 3 N and a coupled sway force 2x - y = -6 N. This is algebraic allocation only, with no actuator limits. Find x and y. Enter exact values as decimals or fractions such as 3/8; tolerance ±0.001.
items.solution: Adding gives 3x = 3 + (-6) = -3, so x = -1 N. Then y = 3 - x = 4 N. Check: 2·(-1) - 4 = -6.
hints: The y-coefficients are +1 and -1, so a single operation removes y.
Add the two equations to eliminate y, then solve the result for x.
Adding gives 3x = 3 + (-6) = -3, so x = -1 N. Then y = 3 - x = 4 N. Check: 2·(-1) - 4 = -6.
items.remediation: If you got x = 3 (y = 0) you added 3 and 6 instead of 3 and -6. A reversed (negative) thruster command is a valid allocation here. Revisit /lessons/M04.

items.prompt: A different thruster layout gives 2x + y = -0.5 N and x - 3y = 5 N for signed commands x and y (N). There are no actuator limits. Find x and y. Enter exact values as decimals or fractions such as 3/8; tolerance ±0.001.
hints: No single addition cancels a variable here; scale one equation first.
Multiply the first equation by 3 so its y-term becomes +3y, then add it to x - 3y = 5.
items.remediation: If x looked right but y did not, recheck the substitution y = -0.5 - 2x; a sign slip there gives y = 0.5. Revisit /lessons/M04.

items.prompt: Two thrusters with signed commands x and y (N) sit at lever arms 0.5 m and 1.5 m, so the net yaw moment is 0.5x + 1.5y = -2.375 N·m. Thruster 1 is a double unit and thruster 2 points backward, so the net force is 2x - y = 4.5 N. There are no actuator limits. Find x and y. Enter exact values as decimals or fractions such as 3/8; tolerance ±0.001.
hints: One equation is a moment (N·m) and one is a force (N); both are linear in the same commands x and y.
Solve the force equation for y (y = 2x - 4.5) and substitute it into the moment equation.
items.remediation: If your values fail the check 2x - y = 4.5, you probably rearranged it as y = 4.5 - 2x; the correct form is y = 2x - 4.5. Revisit /lessons/M04.

routeNotes.sensor-calibration: Fit sensor offset/gain from two calibration points, then undo two-channel crosstalk.
routeNotes.force-allocation: Recover signed thruster commands from coupled force and moment equations.
